wages.text: She voted for AB 1228, legislation establishing minimum-wage standards for fast-food workers.
wages.quote: Allen, Alvarado-Gil, Archuleta, Ashby, Atkins, Becker, Blakespear, Bradford, Caballero, Cortese

safety.text: She advocates prosecuting violence and gun crimes while also investing in mental-health, addiction-treatment and crime-prevention programs.
safety.quote: Public safety means feeling safe, and it starts with stopping crime before it happens and ensuring violence and gun crimes are prosecuted to the fullest extent. I’ll keep working shoulder-to-shoulder with law enforcement while investing in mental health services, addiction treatment, and programs that reduce homelessness and crime before they start.

immigration.text: She called for secure borders while supporting amnesty for undocumented immigrants who work, obey the law and contribute to their communities.
immigration.quote: We should be working to secure our borders‚ invest in order and public safety‚ and create a path to amnesty for those who are hardworking‚ good people.

guns.text: She called for reinstating a national assault-weapons ban.
guns.quote: We had a national assault weapons ban from 1994-2004 and we could have one again. We should demand it.

abortion.text: Her official Senate biography describes her as consistently supportive of abortion rights.
abortion.quote: Catherine has been a champion of women’s reproductive rights since before entering public life.  Catherine is proud to have been 100% pro-choice, 100% of the time.

gender.text: She voted for AB 1955, which protects LGBTQ students’ gender-identity privacy and bars mandatory outing policies in schools.
gender.quote: Allen, Archuleta, Ashby, Atkins, Becker, Blakespear, Bradford, Caballero, Cortese, Dodd, Durazo, Eggman

health.text: She voted for and praised a state budget that maintained planned funding increases for Medi-Cal.
health.quote: It maintains previously planned program increases for schools, higher education, CalWORKs and SSI/SSP grants, Medi-Cal and more.

energy.text: She says accelerating the transition to clean energy and fighting climate change are central goals of her public service.
energy.quote: It’s been my mission in public service to accelerate our transition to clean energy, fight climate change, and safeguard our natural resources for generations to come.

voting.text: She voted for SB 1174, which prohibited local governments from imposing voter-identification requirements beyond state or federal law.
voting.quote: Archuleta, aye. Ashby, aye. Atkins, aye. Becker, aye. Blakespear, aye. Bradford, aye. Caballero, aye. Cortese, aye.

tax.text: Bassett says California should stop imposing new taxes and fees and let residents keep more of their earnings.
tax.quote: That means stopping unnecessary new taxes and fees and letting people keep more of what they earn.

housing.text: Bassett says housing supply should increase by reducing fees, regulations and other barriers to construction.
housing.quote: Excessive fees and regulations have made building new homes far more expensive, slowing construction and driving up the price of every home and every rent check.

safety.text: Bassett says law enforcement and prosecutors need stronger support, adequate resources, and effective enforcement tools.
safety.quote: Law enforcement officers and prosecutors play a crucial role in maintaining order, and they need clear laws, strong support, and the right tools to respond effectively when crime occurs.

sentencing.text: Bassett supports funding Proposition 36 and strengthening penalties for serious drug and firearm offenses and consequences for repeat offenders.
sentencing.quote: Voters overwhelmingly approved Proposition 36 to strengthen penalties for serious drug and firearm offenses and ensure repeat offenders face appropriate consequences.

energy.text: Bassett says she would reduce regulatory barriers that she believes increase energy costs.
energy.quote: As a legislator, I would focus on cutting wasteful spending, opposing new taxes, and reducing regulatory barriers that drive up housing and energy costs so people can keep more of what they earn.
